To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a fully renewable pan-Europe would need a transmission system that is about 4-5 times larger than today's, and that this system should be built up during the ramp-up from 15% to 80%, i.e., during the next 40 years.

(1) transmission grid extensions are required to fully exploit renewable energy resources in Europe; (2) the optimal wind-solar mix changes with increasing transmission; and (3) the optimal wind-to-solar ratio is about 80% wind power in the final VRES-only system, with the remaining 20% coming from solar power.

1) the final need for energy storage can be reduced by up to 33% by a quadrupling of the international transmission capacities; 2) the optimal mix between the two main VRES sources, wind and solar, shifts from 70% to around 80% wind as transmission capacities increase; and 3) the import/export potential of a country depends strongly on the international transmission capacities.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a long-term perspective on the European power system, and it shows how the transmission grid can help reduce the need for backup energy, and how it affects the import and exporting opportunities for single countries.
the question of what is the optimal mix between VRES and transmission investments to achieve a fully renewable power supply in Europe.
the question how the transmission grid can be used to reduce the need for backup energy in a fully VRES-powered European electricity system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the build-up of an entirely VRES-based pan-European electricity supply requires a substantial increase in transmission capacity.
transmission grid reinforcements can significantly reduce backup needs in a fully renewable electricity system, but that the main benefits can be reaped already during the VRES build-up.
the future transmission needs are strongly correlated to the VRES ramp up.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a fully renewable pan-Europe would require a 2.5 to 3-fold increase in today's transmission capacities, depending on the transmission reinforcement strategy.

the transmission grid is an essential part of the future VRES ramp-up and that the transmission grid needs to be enhanced to a large degree to allow for a fully renewable electricity system in Europe.
transmission grid extensions are a necessary step to achieve a fully renewable electricity supply.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a significant reduction in the need for backup power can be achieved by increasing the transmission capacities between countries.
the future need for backup power can be significantly reduced by a moderate increase in transmission capacities.
transmission is a key factor to reduce the need for backup energy, which can be used to reduce the need to store energy or to reduce the need of fossil energy for backup.
